newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican government says rebel actions declined.
newsitem.headline: Mexican government says rebel actions declined.

text.p: The Mexican government said on Tuesday that actions by the leftist rebel Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) had diminished in recent days because of operations by security forces.

"It is clear that even though the activity of the EPR has diminished or has been inhibited by security operations and the general rejection society has shown them, actions of propaganda and intimidation have become their characteristic profile," the interior ministry said in a statement.
False bomb threats had been made in several states in recent days, around the date of Sunday's Independence Day celebrations, but all had turned out to be false alarms, the ministry said.
It confirmed that two soldiers were wounded and one suspected rebel killed in an attack on government troops on Sunday in the southern state of Guerrero, where the EPR first appeared in June.
The body of a 21-year-old farmhand, in military kit and with an AK47 assault rifle nearby, was found near the scene of the attack, authorities said on Tuesday.

Radio station Radio Red reported that an EPR statement released on Tuesday in the southeastern state of Chiapas, dated September 11, called on people there to demand the resignation of the state government and denounced human rights violations.
The statement made no reference to the state's Zapatista rebels, who have asked the EPR to stay out of Chiapas.
The Zapatistas have been in peace talks with the government since April last year, although they suspended the negotiations earlier this month.

Earlier on Tuesday, an official in the southern state of Oaxaca said a small band of suspected EPR rebels staged an Independence Day vigil just 100 yards (metres) from police headquarters in the capital of the state.
Oaxaca Prosecutor Andres Ruiz Cruz told reporters about six suspected members of the EPR dodged tight security and for five minutes paid homage to an independence hero at dawn on Monday.

"Long live the independence heroes - EPR," said a floral banner left in a small park at the foot of a monument to independence fighter and priest, Jose Maria Morelos, Ruiz said. It remained there for five hours before being removed.
